text:
Riley: heads-up — two support tickets where our SDK breaks in Cloudflare/Bun with `Unexpected token 'export'`. They installed normally; bundler picked ESM in a CJS runtime. Anyone have a pragmatic publish pattern?

Jo: this is the classic dual-build/mapping mess. Quick checklist that reduced noise for us before: 1) set a single `types` entry (e.g. `dist/types/index.d.ts`) that re-exports everything, 2) add `typesVersions` for older TS, 3) run `npm pack` smoke installs against node, next-edge, bun before publishing.

Marta: +1. Also consider an explicit edge entry in `exports` like "./edge": { "import": "./dist/edge/index.esm.js" } so docs can point users there if needed. But some bundlers ignore `exports` and prefer `module`/`main` fields.

Riley: what about a companion package `@redwood/inference-edge`? Pros: clear ESM-only semantics and tiny runtime. Cons: more surface area and onboarding friction.

Jo: companion package is safest for customers who want zero surprises. But before we split, do the smoke CI first; if it still fails for a sizable chunk of installs, we open the -edge prototype.

Marta: small TS gotcha — if you put types only inside `exports` conditionals, older `tsc`/IDEs won't find them. Make `types` point to a single file. Example: "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts" where that file `export * from './node'; export * from './shared';`.

Support: FYI two tickets were both Next.js edge functions and one Bun SSR app. Customers confused by docs recommending single package.

BuildBot: created job `ci:pack-smoke` that runs `npm pack` -> install into samples (node, next-edge, bun) and runs minimal require/import checks. Will fail publish if any runtime import throws.

Riley: action items: 1) short-term PR to add `dist/types/index.d.ts` + `typesVersions` and hook `ci:pack-smoke` into publish. 2) mid-term: prototype `@redwood/inference-edge` as ESM-only canary if smoke fails. 3) docs: add a one-paragraph note in onboarding samples explaining edge caveat and the `-edge` package if published.

Jo: I'll open the PR for types and TS mapping. Marta can you own the smoke CI?

Marta: yes, will add the pack+install matrix and include Bun, Next edge, and Node. Also add a tiny script that programmatically does `try { require(...) } catch (e) { process.exit(1) }` and equivalent ESM import checks.

Riley: great — keep PRs small. If smoke still shows failures after the types+CI patch, we'll ship the -edge canary and update samples.

Support: noted, I'll update the affected support tickets with the plan and point customers to the canary if they want immediate workaround. :thumbsup:
